propositions: The generic reads-under-sync-contention property does not subsume test_cli_show_complete_or_erroring_under_write_burst because it misses content-completeness faults (F3: empty-shape-valid payload; F6: missing ticket_id field) that only the original test detects.

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix leaves both burst tests green; only the deterministic held-lock tests detect the regression, meaning the burst test does not protect against its namesake bug.

The two test oracles are mutual complements: the original catches partial-success payload defects (F3, F6); the generic catches stall behaviors (F5) and list-surface defects (F7) that the original misses.

Fault-seeded evidence (seven independently applied defects) establishes that removal of either test would decrease mutation detection score, violating the standard criterion for safe test deletion (Just et al. FSE 2014).

The storm-based tests are inherently weak oracles for specific races by construction; maintained OSS projects (Go, PostgreSQL, CPython) retain narrow deterministic regression tests alongside or instead of probabilistic storm tests.
